def write_noanalysis_reads(in_file, region_file, out_file, config):
    """Write a BAM file of reads in the specified region file that are not analyzed.

    We want to get only reads not in analysis regions but also make use of
    the BAM index to perform well on large files. The tricky part is avoiding
    command line limits. There is a nice discussion on SeqAnswers:
    http://seqanswers.com/forums/showthread.php?t=29538
    sambamba supports intersection via an input BED file so avoids command line
    length issues.
    """
    amba is a good tool for this.

        Args:
            in_file (str): Path to input BAM file.
            region_file (str): Path to BED file containing regions to analyze.
            out_file (str): Path to output BAM file.
            config (dict): The configuration dictionary.
        """
        # Create a temp directory to store the intermediate files.
        temp_dir = os.path.join(config["dirs"]["tmp"], "noanalysis_reads")
        if not os.path.exists(temp_dir):
            os.makedirs(temp_dir)

        # Get the list of regions to analyze.
        regions = get_regions(region_file)

        # Get the list of all the chromosomes in the BAM file.
        chroms = get_chroms(in_file)

        # Make a list of all the chromosomes that are not in the analysis regions.
        chroms_not_in_regions = list(set(chroms) - set(regions))

        # Get the list of chromosomes to analyze.
        chroms_to_analyze = list(set(chroms) & set(regions))

        # Write a BED file of the regions not to analyze.
        noanalysis_bed = os.path.join(temp_dir, "noanalysis.bed")

        noanalysis_bam = os.path.join(temp_dir, "noanalysis.bam")
